meta.name: HLD — kept deliberately light
meta.desc: At ~1 YoE, HLD rounds are shallow: know the vocabulary, sketch 8 classics, don't over-invest. One page, done.

concepts.title: Vertical vs horizontal scaling
Load balancers: L4 vs L7, round-robin vs least-connections, health checks
Caching: cache-aside vs write-through vs write-back; eviction (LRU/LFU/TTL)
Cache problems: stampede, hot keys, invalidation
CDN: what it caches, push vs pull, when it matters
DNS: resolution path, TTL, GeoDNS
Sharding: hash vs range, resharding pain, consistent hashing
Replication: leader-follower, sync vs async, replication lag
SQL vs NoSQL: when each, document vs KV vs wide-column vs graph
Indexes: what they cost on writes, composite indexes
CAP theorem + PACELC in one breath; eventual vs strong consistency
Message queues: Kafka vs RabbitMQ vs SQS mental model; pub/sub vs work queue
Idempotency: idempotency keys, why retries demand it
Rate limiting: token bucket, sliding window, where to enforce
WebSockets vs long polling vs SSE
API design: REST semantics, pagination, versioning, HTTP status codes
API gateway vs reverse proxy vs load balancer (untangle the three)
Microservices vs monolith: real tradeoffs at small-team scale
Object storage (S3) vs block vs file; presigned URLs
Blob/media pipeline: upload → transcode → CDN (the YouTube-lite spine)
Back-of-envelope: QPS, storage, bandwidth — memorize the powers-of-ten table
Availability math: 99.9 vs 99.99, SLA/SLO/SLI, single points of failure
Distributed ID generation: auto-increment vs UUID vs Snowflake
Transactions across services: sagas, outbox pattern (recognition level)
Observability: metrics vs logs vs traces; what you'd alert on
